newsitem.title: USA: Zenith supports rapid launch of HDTV.
newsitem.headline: Zenith supports rapid launch of HDTV.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp, on the heels of last week's landmark digital television decisions by the Federal Communications Commission, said Monday it is helping broadcasters prepare for the rapid launch of digital high-definition television (HDTV).

In a report issued from Las Vegas, Zenith noted that multiple over-the-air broadcasts of digital HDTV are expected to be the technological highlight of this year's National Association of Broadcasters (NAB) convention, and Zenith's digital equipment and technical expertise will figure prominently in each of these HDTV transmissions.

"Zenith's goal at NAB '97 is to actively support the broadcast equipment industry in its early introduction of new digital transmitters and related products, and to help drive a rapid, orderly transition to digital TV broadcasting," said Paul Snopko, director of research and development.

"We're greatly encouraged by the number of digital product introductions at this week's NAB, and our timetable calls for the shipment of first-generation HDTV receivers to major-market retailers beginning in 1998," Snopko noted.
In Las Vegas, Zenith is engaged in cooperative efforts with six transmitter manufacturers.

In addition to the HDTV activities generated by individual transmitter manufacturers, Zenith also is supporting the inter-industry Advanced Television Systems Committee (ATSC) plans to conduct what has been described as "the first transcontinental broadcast of digital HDTV."
Glenview, Ill.-based Zenith manufactures and markets television and video products, display devices and network systems products. ((Reuters Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
